title: Music Composition and Audio Engineering
answer: Score generation, stem separation, drum programming, mixing and mastering, and generated foley.

children.name: Score Generation and Composition
children.blurb: Score generation and composition covers systems that produce musical notation, MIDI, or full scores from text prompts, existing motifs, or harmonic constraints.

children.name: Stem Separation and Restoration
children.blurb: Stem separation and restoration covers splitting a mixed recording into isolated sources such as vocals, drums, bass, and other instruments, and repairing degraded audio by reducing noise, clicks, clipping, and reverberation.

children.name: Generative Rhythm and Drum Programming
children.blurb: Generative rhythm and drum programming covers AI systems that create drum patterns, fills, and full percussion arrangements from user inputs such as tempo, genre, feel, or an existing musical phrase.

children.name: Automated Mixing and Mastering
children.blurb: Automated mixing and mastering uses machine learning to set levels, equalization, compression, stereo image, and loudness for recorded music, either as assistive tools or fully autonomous processing.

children.name: Generated Foley and Sound Design
children.blurb: Generated foley and sound design covers AI systems that create or manipulate sound effects, ambiences, footsteps, cloth, impacts, and other non-musical audio for film, television, games, and interactive media.

sections.body: This field covers software that writes musical scores, separates recordings into individual instrument or vocal parts, programs drum patterns, adjusts mixes and masters, and creates sound effects. Current AI systems do these tasks with neural networks trained on large collections of audio and symbolic music. Score generation tools can produce short melodic or harmonic passages in a chosen style, while stem separation tools split a finished song into vocals, bass, drums, and other elements. Drum programming models generate rhythm patterns that fit a given tempo or genre. Mixing and mastering tools apply equalization, compression, and loudness adjustments automatically. Generated foley systems create footsteps, cloth rustles, or ambient room tone from text or visual cues.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven across these five areas. Stem separation is the most mature, with several tools producing usable separations for common pop and rock recordings, though bleed and artifacts remain on dense or heavily effected material. Score generation can imitate short passages but struggles with long form structure, motivic development, and emotional intent. Automated mixing and mastering can match reference loudness and basic tonal balance, yet professional engineers still correct many decisions on complex or dynamic material. Drum programming is reliable for simple loops but less convincing for human feel, fills, or unusual time signatures, and generated foley is improving for common sounds but often fails on rare or physically complex events. The site tracks 2000 audio models, and 18 of the 92 active intellectual property lawsuits involve AI music services, which reflects unresolved questions about training data and ownership.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader interested in melody and harmony would start with Score Generation and Composition, which covers how models create original musical material. Someone working with existing recordings would turn to Stem Separation and Restoration for tools that isolate or repair individual parts. Generative Rhythm and Drum Programming is the page for beat making and percussion patterns, while Automated Mixing and Mastering addresses the final polish of a track. Generated Foley and Sound Design covers non musical sound effects for film, games, and other media. Together these pages move from creating musical ideas to separating, arranging, and finishing audio, with foley as a separate branch for sound effects.
